pr_body:
Whenever a search timeout is set to a search request, the timeout may be triggered by the suggest phase via exitable directory reader. In that case, the exception that is thrown by the timeout check needs to be handled, instead of returned back to the user.

Instead of handling the timeout in each phase, this commit handles it as part of QueryPhase for both SuggestPhase and RescorePhase.

For rescore phase, one integration test that is time dependent is also rewritten to remove the time dependency and moved from QueryRescorerIT to SearchTimeoutIT.

Closes #122186

issue_context.title: Query timeout fails for suggest and rescore phases
issue_context.body:
The `_search` request timeout enforces an early termination for queries exceeding their allocated time budget. This timeout is applied per shard and only affects the query phase, ensuring that a partial response can still be returned when triggered.  

However, [PR #98715](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/98715) modified this behavior by removing the timeout restriction for the aggregation build phase but did not account for the suggest and rescore phases. As a result, queries that exceed their timeout now throw an unexpected exception (`time_exceeded_exception`) when running additional phases that are not setup to handle timeouts.

oh boy I did not realize it was that easy to reproduce, thank you! I had similar cases in the past from the fetch phase, but they were much harder to reproduce. I will look into this!
What surprise me is that it returns a 500 instead of a 429.

That's because `TimeExceededException` should never be returned to users, but rather caught internally and handled. Not the first time this happens I think, that is why we restored a stacktrace for this exception (by restoring the fill stacktrace method), which should not be needed in theory, but it becomes impossible to track down where we miss to handle it without a stacktrace.
From looking at the code, the suggest phase is definitely affected, but I think that the rescore phase isn't as it was fixed with #115048 .

review_comments: Maybe add an overload to this method that just takes a `searchContext`? Removes some duplication and keeps the cold path code size down :)
That is an option, I think back when I added it I wanted to not make the method depend on the entire context, which exposes all kinds of stuff.
